conclusion: We study recombination-sensitive branch structure on a fixed-support substrate in Six Birds Theory. Building on prior work on event packaging and predictive holonomy, we introduce branch assemblages and two quotient levels at an interface: a branchwise predictive quotient ( K_i ), which captures independent predictive treatment of the branches, and a recombination quotient ( R_i ), which captures admissible recombination observables on branch families. On this architecture we exhibit a benchmark suite separating classical mixture, hidden predictive memory without recombination sensitivity, route-marked suppression, erasure-conditioned recovery, cyclic-family generalization, dissipative washout, and artifact controls based on protocol internalization and flattening/completion. A supporting theorem layer proves the abstract factorized no-interference regime and its obstruction by strict refinement, and one promoted positive family is connected to a theorem-backed concrete witness in an aligned Lean model. We do not claim a general reconstruction of non-Hilbert interference or a formalization of the full benchmark runtime. The claim is narrower: these recombination phenomena arise on fixed support, can be audited exactly, and admit a partial formal backbone on the Six Birds substrate.

conclusion: The previous sections are empirical. This section records the supporting theorem layer established in the Lean development. Its role is interpretive: it identifies the abstract no-interference regime, proves that strict refinement obstructs that regime, and supplies one theorem-backed concrete positive instance for an aligned Lean model of the strongest promoted family. It is not a formalization of the full benchmark runtime. The supporting formal development is implemented in Lean . At the level of mathematical form, quotient descent, factorization through quotients, and state separation by observables are standard patterns; see, for example, . The contribution here is their use in the present fixed-support substrate and benchmark program. Two explicit assumption packages organize the abstract theorem layer. The first is a detectability assumption: branchwise summaries are visible through a distinguished observable layer that separates them. The second is a global factorization assumption: every admissible recombination observable factors through the branchwise summary. Under these assumptions, the Lean development proves the following backbone results.

conclusion: The paper establishes a substrate-level result. On a fixed-support Six Birds architecture, branchwise predictive structure and recombination-sensitive structure can be separated operationally, and that separation can be audited under exact finite controls. The benchmark suite shows that the same substrate supports a classical-mixture null regime, hidden predictive memory without additional recombination sensitivity, readable-route suppression, erased conditional recovery, bounded cyclic-family generalization, dissipative washout, and artifact controls based on protocol internalization and flattening/completion. The formal contribution is narrower. The Lean development proves an abstract refinement layer under detectability, a factorized no-interference regime in which the recombination quotient collapses to the branchwise quotient, and the corresponding obstruction result that strict refinement rules out global branchwise factorization. It also proves one theorem-backed concrete positive instance for an aligned Lean model of the promoted family n5_d1_w1of4_3of4 . These results support the interpretation of the benchmark suite but do not replace it.

expanded_source_wording_tex: What the paper does \emph{not} establish is equally important. It does not provide a reconstruction of quantum theory, and it does not claim to be the first general treatment of interference beyond Hilbert-space formalisms; generalized-measure and operational/GPT frameworks already provide broader settings for such questions \cite{Sorkin1994QuantumMeasure,Barrett2007GPT,BarnumMuellerUdudec2014HigherOrder,LeeSelby2017HigherOrder,DakicPaterekBrukner2014DensityCubes,GarnerEtAl2013PhaseInterference,Plavala2023GPTIntro,ChiribellaDarianoPerinotti2011InformationalDerivation}. Nor is the paper a contribution to the separate program of testing or characterizing higher-order interference in the Sorkin hierarchy and its operational extensions \cite{SinhaEtAl2010RulingOutMultiOrder,UdudecBarnumEmerson2011ThreeSlit,DakicPaterekBrukner2014DensityCubes,LeeSelby2017HigherOrder}. It does not prove the paired erasure benchmark in full runtime detail, the full cyclic-family generalization, or the dissipative control. Those results remain empirical exact-finite evidence. Likewise, route readability and visibility recovery remain concrete diagnostics in the computational layer rather than formal objects on the Lean side.
